title: One question at a time
statement: Ask one thing at a time: one question per screen, and a two-part task as two turns, so the feedback can answer each part.
example: Three pages overflowed the screen for the same reason: two choice questions stacked on one page.
detail: A one-screen census at 1440×900 found four pages too tall, three of them for the same reason, two multiple-choice questions stacked on one page; each was split into single-question pages with every quoted option kept. A reading course's vocabulary rulebook splits saying a word and defining it into two separate turns, because one question asking both complicates the feedback when a child gets both parts wrong.
against: the two-turn split is built into the card's structure, but no validator checks it.

evidence.quote: two MCQs stacked on one page

the defect is SIMULTANEITY, not existence.
